subject: Boot rooms and practical entrance storage
hook: Our hallway is narrow. Is there any point in a boot bench?
fb:
Lots of terraced and semi-detached houses round here have long, narrow hallways, and we often hear: is there any point trying to fit storage in ours?

There usually is. Because everything we make is built to measure, a bench or shoe cabinet can be made shallower than shop-bought furniture so there's still room to walk past. The space under the stairs, the wall behind the front door and slim wall-hung storage are all worth a look too.

We start by measuring the width and checking which way the doors open, then design around that. If your hallway is a squeeze, send us a question or book a free consultation:
https://superiofurniture.com/contact/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=productive-spaces-and-home-offices&utm_content=day-245
gbp:
Our hallway is narrow. Can we still have entrance storage?

In most cases, yes. Shop-bought benches and shoe cabinets come in standard depths that can block a narrow hallway. Made-to-measure furniture doesn't have to: a bench, shoe cabinet or coat cupboard can be built shallower so there's still comfortable room to walk past.

Other options that often suit narrow entrances include slim wall-hung coat storage, a tall cupboard behind the front door where it doesn't block the swing, and storage built into the space under the stairs.

We always start by measuring the clear width of the hallway and checking which way every door opens, then design around those limits. Everything is made in our own Hanley workshop and fitted by our own team.

Book a free, no-obligation design consultation to see what will fit your entrance.
